theorem: Over RCA_0, conventional compactly supported smooth-test names with discrete support advice are uniformly equivalent to a tagged support-indexed union of fixed-support smooth names. The fixed-stage translators coherently embed every such named test into the rational H2 carrier and assemble the coded weak identity, while equality with the full locally convex LF topology remains explicitly unestablished.

support_exhaustion.nesting: K_j is contained in the interior of K_(j+1)
support_exhaustion.coverage: every compact subset of the open unit cylinder is contained in some K_j

represented_union.name: pair (j,p), where j is a support-stage tag and p is a fixed-support smooth derivative name at K_j
represented_union.equivalence: (j,p) and (k,q) agree when their images agree in a common stage K_m with m>=j,k
represented_union.inclusion: i_jk preserves the represented function and changes only its admissible support bound

name_comparison.choice_use: NONE: the support bound is copied, not selected

h2_embedding.inclusion_compatibility: outputs from different valid support tags are equivalent H2 names of the same test
h2_embedding.weak_residual: zero for every represented-union smooth-test name

topology_comparison.classical_object: the locally convex strict inductive-limit test-function space D=C_c-infinity
topology_comparison.represented_object: the quotient representation carried by a discrete support tag and a fixed-stage name
topology_comparison.point_name_equivalence: PROVED for the declared conventional and tagged representations
topology_comparison.reason: point-name translations and sequential convergence data do not by themselves certify the full locally convex LF universal property; the H2 completion also contains nonsmooth H2 elements

formal_proof.statement: The rational compact stages K_j=[2^-(j+2),1-2^-(j+2)] times the circle are nested, their interiors exhaust the open unit cylinder, and K_j has a rational collar inside K_(j+1).

A name in the represented union is a natural support tag j together with a fixed-support smooth derivative name at K_j; two names denote the same test when their fixed-stage names agree after inclusion into some common later stage.

A conventional represented bump/test name consisting of a smooth name plus a discrete compact-support bound translates to the tagged pair by rebracketing, and conversely. Both composites preserve the name fields exactly, so no support bound is selected.

At each stage, the certified cubic collar translator supplies a rational fast H2 name. If the same smooth test is retagged at a later support stage, both output names converge to that test and are equivalent in the H2 completion with the sum of their explicit rates.
The exact coded weak-wave residual therefore vanishes for every test carrying a represented-union name, independently of the chosen sufficiently large support tag.

The name equivalence concerns represented points and stage inclusions. It does not prove that the induced represented topology equals the full classical locally convex LF topology, and the H2 embedding is not a bicontinuous identification or a single metric completion of C_c-infinity.

literature_context.citation: Arno Pauly and Florian Steinberg, Comparing Representations for Function Spaces in Computable Analysis, Theory of Computing Systems 62 (2018), 557-582
literature_context.role: Primary representation context for smooth functions, bump functions, test functions, and discrete support advice.
literature_context.import_boundary: The local certificate proves only the displayed name translations and does not import an LF-topology equivalence theorem.

equality between the represented quotient topology and the full classical locally convex LF topology
surjectivity of the smooth-test embedding onto the H2 completion
a single metrization or metric completion of the classical test-function LF space
causal Green propagation, a Weyl equation, or a metric-BV theorem
